family.description: This domain is found at the C terminus of proteins such as the probable glycosyltransferase Gly ([swissprot:Q9AEU2]) that also contain the glycosyl transferase domain at the N terminus. It is also found N-terminal in numerous putative glycosyltransferases such as GalT1. GalT1 has been shown to catalyse the third step of Fap1 glycosylation [[cite:PUB00081880]]. This domain is structurally distinct from all known GT folds of glycosyltransferases and contains a metal binding site. This new glycosyltransferase fold has been named GT-D [[cite:PUB00081880]].
family.name: Glycosyltransferase GT-D fold
